findings.diagnosis: The prompt routinely treats a following clausal or complement continuation as safe to cut off — it allows cuts immediately before spans that actually complete or disambiguate the preceding predicate or noun, producing contradiction, lost scope, or orphaned dependents when pieces are translated separately.
findings.evidence: en_us_733, en_us_378, en_us_1507, en_us_1294, en_us_721, en_us_1617, en_us_1116, en_us_360, en_us_174, en_us_1294. These sentences all show the policy keeping a cut immediately before a short continuation (relative/complement clause, prepositional complement, or quoted multiword complement) whose content is required to finish the prior predicate/NP; the offline targets keep that continuation attached and recover cohesion / avoid contradiction.
findings.type_predicate: Sentences where the span immediately after a candidate cut is a clausal or complement continuation that syntactically completes or disambiguates the immediately preceding predicate or noun (relative/complement clause, essential prepositional complement, or quoted multiword complement).

edit.text: Do not cut immediately before a following span that syntactically completes or disambiguates the preceding predicate or noun (relative/complement clauses, essential prepositional complements, or quoted multiword complements).
